column3: Liu Bei (Xuande) of the Chinese Three Kingdoms era, now about thirty-eight, just after he watched Lu Bu executed at the White Gate Tower and now lives as Cao Cao's guest in Xuchang. He has passed from youth into early middle age: faint lines at the corners of the eyes and between the brows, cheeks a little leaner, the moustache and goatee fuller and longer. FACE: the same face as in the reference, but the earnest openness of his youth is gone; the eyes are calm, guarded and unreadable, a courteous composed mouth that reveals nothing, a quiet shrewdness and a new hardness beneath the politeness; a man who has learned to hide his heart. Black cap with the small gold hairpin on his topknot, the same green robe with plain ivory lapel bands, a dark sash. He stands with his hands joined inside his sleeves in a polite courtier's posture, body bowed very slightly, but his eyes glance sideways past the viewer, three-quarter view facing left. Background in light ink wash: the tall eaves of a capital palace and a distant gate tower under a pale overcast sky, faint.

Liu Bei (Xuande) of the Chinese Three Kingdoms era, now a warlord about forty-eight, ruler of his own lands. Middle-aged: deep lines on the forehead and beside the nose, a long black beard and moustache streaked with a little grey, a heavier, more imposing frame. FACE: the same face as in the reference, aged, but now with the cold imposing air of a hegemon very like Cao Cao: heavy-lidded eyes that look down and weigh men like pieces, a firm unsmiling mouth, ambition and ruthless resolve; dignified, formidable and a little frightening. A black cap with a gold crown ornament, a deep dark green robe with gold trim, dark steel shoulder armour, a red-black sash. He stands tall with one hand resting on the hilt of a long sword planted before him, the other hand closed in a fist at his side, looking down at the viewer, front view turned slightly left. Background in light ink wash: massed army banners without writing on steep mountain passes under storm clouds, faint.

Liu Bei (Xuande) of the Chinese Three Kingdoms era, now about forty-seven, middle-aged, still holding to the ideal he swore under the peach trees. Faint lines at the eyes and brow, a longer black beard and moustache with a trace of grey at the temples, a lean upright frame. FACE: the same face as in the reference, aged, with clear deep steady eyes full of conviction, level brows, a firm closed mouth; resolute and unbending yet graceful and serene; strength that comes from belief, a man who has endured many defeats without losing his way. Black cap with the small gold hairpin, a flowing green robe with plain ivory lapel bands and long wide sleeves stirred by the wind, a simple sword at his waist. He stands with one hand raised slightly before him, palm open, as if inviting someone forward, gazing far into the distance, three-quarter view facing left. Background in light ink wash: spring fields and terraced farmland under clearing morning light with river mist and distant mountains, faint.

Guan Yu (Yunchang) of the Chinese Three Kingdoms era, now about thirty-nine. Early middle age: the same red face and long black beard as in the reference, a few deeper lines at the brow, the beard even longer. FACE: the same face as in the reference, but his calm has turned to smouldering anger: narrow phoenix eyes now opened and burning, thick brows drawn hard together, nostrils flared, jaw clenched; a proud quick-tempered man who barely restrains his wrath, with the first shadow of arrogance. Green headscarf, green robe over armour with gold trim. He grips the long shaft of his crescent-bladed Green Dragon glaive in one fist, the blade rising beside his head, the other hand gripping the end of his beard, turned three-quarter right toward the viewer as if someone has insulted him. Background in light ink wash: dark rain sweeping across a river crossing with bending reeds, faint.

Guan Yu (Yunchang) of the Chinese Three Kingdoms era, now about fifty-eight, the great general guarding Jing province at the height of his fame, in his final year. Middle-aged and weathered: the same red face as in the reference, deep lines, the very long beard now streaked with grey, a powerful heavy frame. FACE: the same face as in the reference, aged, with supreme arrogance: chin lifted, half-closed phoenix eyes looking down the nose with cold disdain, a contemptuous set mouth; a man who believes no one under heaven is his equal. Green headscarf with a gold ornament, a magnificent green robe over gilded armour. He sits upright on a campaign seat, holding an open bamboo book of the Spring and Autumn Annals in one hand without bothering to look at the viewer, the Green Dragon glaive leaning upright behind him, three-quarter view facing left. Background in light ink wash: a swollen river in flood beneath a city wall and dark autumn clouds, faint.

Zhang Fei (Yide) of the Chinese Three Kingdoms era, now about thirty-four. Older than in the reference: a heavier, more battle-worn frame, a small scar across one cheekbone, the bristling tiger beard thicker and wilder. FACE: the same face as in the reference, but harsher and more violent: round eyes bloodshot and blazing, brows knotted, lips pulled back from clenched teeth in a savage snarl (not open-mouthed shouting), veins standing on the temple; a man whose temper now explodes into brutality. Bare black topknot with a red band, a green robe with dark iron shoulder guards, a red sash, sleeves rolled to show thick forearms. He holds the serpent spear diagonally across his body with both fists as if about to strike, leaning forward toward the viewer, body turned three-quarter left. Background in light ink wash: smoke and scattered broken banners over a trampled field, faint.

Zhang Fei (Yide) of the Chinese Three Kingdoms era, now about fifty-two, a grim veteran general. Middle-aged and battle-hardened: the same broad swarthy face as in the reference with deep lines and old scars, the bristling tiger beard streaked with grey, a massive heavy frame. FACE: the same face as in the reference, aged, cruel and harsh: round eyes cold and merciless under heavy brows, a hard down-turned mouth; a feared commander who flogs his own soldiers and is quick to violence. Black topknot with a red band, dark heavy iron armour over a green robe, a red sash. He holds a coiled leather whip in one fist across his chest, the serpent spear upright behind his shoulder, glaring at the viewer, three-quarter view facing right. Background in light ink wash: a gloomy army camp at dusk with a punishment post and cold wind, faint.

Cao Cao (Mengde) of the Chinese Three Kingdoms era, now about twenty-eight, a young Han officer before the campaign against Dong Zhuo, still a man of ideals who wants to restore the Han. Younger than in the reference: smooth firm skin, a lean frame, only a thin young moustache and very short goatee. FACE: the same face structure as in the reference, but younger and open: bright earnest eyes, a straight determined gaze, a firm hopeful mouth; sharp and clever, proud and upright, a righteous young official, no cunning and no cruelty in the face. Black scholar's cap with a small blue hairpin, a plain blue official's robe with light steel shoulder guards and a red sash, a sword at his hip. He stands upright holding the sword sheathed vertically before his chest in both hands, as if swearing an oath, looking slightly upward past the viewer, three-quarter view facing right. Background in light ink wash: the imperial capital's palace roofs at dawn with smoke rising, faint.

Cao Cao (Mengde) of the Chinese Three Kingdoms era, now about fifty-five, the old master of the north. Older than in the reference: grey streaks in the hair, a longer moustache and beard gone half grey, deep lines around the eyes and mouth, a slightly heavier settled frame. FACE: the same face as in the reference, aged into a wily old fox: hooded half-lidded eyes that see through everyone, a faint unreadable set of the lips, utterly calm, patient and dangerous; seasoned cunning rather than open cruelty. A black court cap with a gold ornament, a rich dark blue robe with gold trim and a dark fur-trimmed mantle over the shoulders, a red sash. He sits leaning back in a carved chair, one elbow on the armrest and two fingers resting at his temple, watching the viewer sidelong, three-quarter view facing right. Background in light ink wash: a towering terrace pavilion with a bronze bird on its roof under evening clouds, faint.

Cao Cao (Mengde) of the Chinese Three Kingdoms era, now about forty-four, the hegemon who holds the Emperor and has begun to crush every rival by deceit and terror. Older than in the reference: a few lines on the brow and at the eyes, a fuller black moustache and beard, a harder frame. FACE: the same face as in the reference, but darker: cold narrow eyes without mercy, a slight cruel tightening at the corner of the mouth (not a smile), a face that hides plots and would rather betray the world than be betrayed; ruthless, deceitful and imposing. A black cap with a gold ornament, black-lacquered steel armour over a deep blue robe, a blood-red cloak, a red sash. He holds his sword half drawn from its scabbard at his hip, looking down at the viewer over his shoulder, three-quarter view facing right. Background in light ink wash: a burning walled city and crows in a smoke-darkened sky, faint.

Cao Cao (Mengde) of the Chinese Three Kingdoms era, now about fifty-six, the aging tyrant who rules in the Emperor's name. Clearly older than in the reference: hair and beard heavily grey, deep lines, sunken cheeks with hard bones, a still strong frame. FACE: the same face as in the reference, aged: heavy-lidded narrow eyes that are cold, suspicious and weary, a thin hard mouth; an old wolf whose cunning and cruelty have become second nature, gripping power with both hands. A black royal cap with a gold crown plate, a black robe embroidered with gold over a dark purple inner robe, a dark fur mantle. He stands at a terrace railing, both hands resting on the pommel of a long sword planted before him, turning his head to look at the viewer, three-quarter view facing left. Background in light ink wash: a grand terrace pavilion with a bronze bird on the roof and a storm gathering over a river, faint.
